title: Independently validating Bayesian scaling laws for in-context learning safety re-emergence

original_idea.body: Independently validating Bayesian scaling laws for ICL (arXiv:2410.16531): fit refusal-probability vs many-shot count on an open safety-tuned model and predict shots needed to re-surface suppressed behavior.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Predictably overriding safety training via many-shot is a concrete, defensible jailbreak-robustness chain.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Inference-only refusal-probability sweeps + curve fitting; guided execution feasible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused fitted-scaling-curve deliverable with held-out validation; bounded.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Auditing jailbreak limits on open safety-tuned models, no training, independent-friendly.

novelty.reasoning: Source paper already predicts re-emergence; independent validation is a partly-open angle.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Prediction exists in source; independent validation may be open.
